title: Flow testing, debugging, versioning, deployment, and production support
objectives: Debug a Flow in Flow Builder and read element-level results before activation.
Create and run automated Flow tests, including Setup Application Test Execution alongside Apex tests where available.
Explain versions: activating a version deactivates the previous one; running interviews continue on the version they started.
Deploy Flows knowing an active Flow in a change set arrives inactive unless the production deploy-as-active setting is used, and activate after deploy.
diagnostic_question: A Flow works in sandbox Debug but not after a change-set deploy. What version is active in production, and what does Help say about deploying an active Flow?
definition: Flow testing is Debug plus automated Flow tests that you can run in Builder or, in later APIs, with Apex tests in Application Test Execution. Versioning means one active version; activating another deactivates the prior, while in-flight interviews keep the version they started. Deployment via change sets typically delivers an active Flow as inactive; you activate in the destination (or use the production setting that allows deploying a new active version). Production support is Debug, tests, versions, and paused-interview awareness—not editing live production as the first move. ([Activate a Flow](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_activate.htm); [Special Behavior in Deployments](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.deploy_special_behavior.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers ask why production is inactive after deploy, whether running interviews jump versions, and how you test record-triggered Flows. ‘I clicked Activate in sandbox so production is live’ is a fail.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a theater. Debug and Flow tests are dress rehearsal. Versions are understudies: only one cast is on stage (active), but a show that already started keeps its original cast (running interviews). Deployment is the touring company: Help says an active Flow in a change set usually arrives inactive—you still have to raise the curtain in the new house. Production support is the stage manager’s headset, not rewriting the script mid-show.
deeper_explanation: Activate Help: when you activate a version, any previously active version is deactivated. Running interviews continue on the version they started. After moving a Flow from sandbox to production you may need to save as a new version before Activate; always debug using rollback mode after that move because orgs differ. ([Activate](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_activate.htm))

Change sets: you can include only one version of a Flow. If there is no active version, the latest inactive is used. An active Flow in a change set is deployed to its destination as inactive. Activate manually after deployment. Deploying creates a version in the destination. Production orgs can enable deploying a new active version via change sets or Metadata API; that setting does not appear in non-production orgs because you can always deploy a new active version there. ([Special Behavior](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.deploy_special_behavior.htm))

Debug in Flow Builder shows element details; later releases added element-level summaries and an updated screen-flow debugger. Debug is not a substitute for automated Flow tests or a bulk Data Loader rehearsal (AUTO-007). ([Debug summaries](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_automate_flow_debug_summaries.htm))

Winter/Spring releases unified Flow tests with Apex tests: Test Discovery / Test Runner APIs (API 65.0+) and Setup Application Test Execution to run both. Application Test History may still show only async Apex history—Needs verification of Flow history UI. CLI: `flow run test` / `flow get test` in later Salesforce CLI notes. ([Unified testing](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_automate_flow_debug_unified_testing.htm))

Production support: reproduce in sandbox, compare active versions, check paused interviews, fault emails (AUTO-008), and whether the change set omitted the version you thought. Do not Debug against real customer data as the first step.

mental_model.analogy: A theater: Debug/tests = dress rehearsal, versions = understudies (one cast on stage), running interviews = a show that keeps its original cast, deploy = touring company that arrives with the curtain down unless you raise it.
useful_mapping: Debug → dress rehearsal on the sandbox stage
automated Flow test → recorded rehearsal you can rerun
inactive versions → understudies on the bench
running interview → a show that already started on its original cast
change set deploy → touring company arriving inactive
Activate in destination → raise the curtain
Flow metadata → the script; records → the audience/ticket data
where_it_breaks: The production deploy-as-active setting can raise the curtain automatically—confirm it is enabled before you assume inactive.
Saving as a new version after sandbox-to-prod is a Help caution, not every deploy path.
CLI test commands are versioned; do not invent flags.
Debug As user is not a full security test (AUTO-009).

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I Debug and run Flow tests in sandbox, then activate. Activating B deactivates A, but running interviews stay on A. A change set usually lands inactive in production; I activate there. I do not treat sandbox Activate as production go-live.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from Help: one version in a change set, active becomes inactive at the destination unless the production deploy-as-active setting is on. I compare version numbers in both orgs. I use Application Test Execution when we have automated Flow tests. For incidents I reproduce in sandbox, check paused interviews, and read fault emails. I debug with rollback after sandbox-to-prod because Help says orgs differ. The script is metadata; tickets are data.

terminology.example: Debug an Opportunity update to Closed Won and read Get Records count.
terminology.non_example: Editing the Flow in production while users run it.

terminology.plain: A saved automated test for a (usually record-triggered) Flow you can rerun.

terminology.example: Test: Stage changes to Closed Won creates two Tasks.
terminology.non_example: A single manual Debug you did not save.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex unit test: different metadata, now launchable in the same Setup page.
terminology.boundary: Not every Flow type supports the same test features—verify in-org.

terminology.plain: One saved edition of the Flow. Only one version is active.
terminology.precise: Activate deactivates the previous. Change sets carry one version. Deploy creates a version in the destination.

terminology.non_example: A Process Builder version from AUTO-012.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: API version on the Flow: runtime behavior version, not the saved-version number.

terminology.precise: Help: activating a version deactivates any previously active version.

terminology.plain: A Flow run that already started, including paused screen or waited interviews.

terminology.non_example: The next user who clicks the button after activate—they get v3.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Paused Flow interviews in Setup: operational list, neighboring UI.

terminology.plain: Sending a Flow version to another org with a change set.

terminology.confusable_neighbor: Metadata API / CLI project deploy: read current special-behavior notes for status.

terminology.plain: A production setting that allows a deploy to activate a new Flow version.
terminology.precise: Help: available in production orgs; not shown in scratch/sandbox/developer orgs because those can always deploy a new active version.

interview_questions.question: How do you test a Flow before activation?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Debug in Flow Builder and read element summaries. Save automated Flow tests and run them—Application Test Execution can run them with Apex tests. Then activate.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do a happy path, a fault path, and at least a small multi-record rehearsal if it is record-triggered (AUTO-007). I do not treat Debug as enough for go-live. I mention API 65+ unified tests without inventing History-page behavior. I activate only the version I tested.
interview_questions.example: Debug Closed Won, save a Flow test that expects two Tasks, run it in Application Test Execution.
tradeoffs: Manual Debug vs automated Flow tests

interview_questions.question: What happens when you activate a new Flow version?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The previous version deactivates. New interviews use the new version. Interviews already running stay on the version they started.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Activate Help. I plan communication for screen Flows and paused interviews. I check the Related versions list, not only the canvas. I mention you may need a new save after sandbox-to-prod before Activate, and to Debug in rollback mode because orgs differ.
interview_questions.example: Activate v5; a user mid-wizard remains on v4 until they finish.
tradeoffs: Breaking change vs waiting for interviews to drain
follow_ups: How do you find paused interviews?
weak_answer_warnings: Everyone instantly gets the new version including in-flight

interview_questions.question: Change set deployed. Production behavior unchanged. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Open production versions. The new version is probably Inactive. Activate it, or confirm deploy-as-active was off. Also confirm the change set carried the intended version.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare version numbers. If no active version was in the set, Help says the latest inactive was uploaded—maybe the wrong one. I check dependencies. I Debug in a full sandbox rather than editing production. I do not rebuild from scratch as step one.
interview_questions.example: v4 Inactive in production; v2 still Active.
follow_ups: How do you prevent this next time?

interview_questions.question: You cannot click Activate on a Flow just moved into production. What does Help say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Save it as a new version first, then Activate. Debug in rollback mode because sandbox and production differ.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat this as a documented org-difference issue, not a corrupt Flow. I check my permissions. I do not copy XML by hand to ‘fix’ Activate. After it is active I rerun tests if they deployed. I watch in-flight interviews.
interview_questions.example: Change-set Flow requires Save As New Version before the Activate button enables.
tradeoffs: Extra version number vs staying inactive
follow_ups: Does Metadata API have the same quirk?

interview_questions.question: How should a team run Flow tests in CI?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Use automated Flow tests and the Test Discovery/Test Runner APIs (65.0+) or CLI `flow run test` as documented for your CLI version. Do not rely on a human Debug in CI.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite the unified-testing note and the CLI weekly note without inventing flags. I keep tests on LAB_ data. I still run a sandbox Debug for new UX. I do not claim Application Test History shows Flow results if the note said it does not yet. Apex tests that invoke Flows are a neighboring pattern I would verify.
interview_questions.example: Pipeline calls Test Runner for Flow plus Apex after deploy to a scratch org.
tradeoffs: Builder tests vs Apex-invoked Flow tests

interview_questions.question: Users report the old screen after you activated a new version an hour ago.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Ask if they started the interview before Activate. Those runs stay on the old version. New starts should be new. Also check they are on the right Lightning page/Flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at paused interviews. I do not immediately deactivate. I confirm Active version in Setup. I may ask them to cancel and restart if the business allows. I treat this as expected Help behavior, not a cache myth only—though I still rule out a second Flow on the page.
interview_questions.example: Service console screen Flow started at 9:00; you activated v6 at 9:10.
tradeoffs: Force cancel vs let them finish
Deactivate entirely during a breaking change
follow_ups: How long can a paused interview live?
weak_answer_warnings: Activate failed because of cache only

interview_questions.question: Metadata versus data in testing and deploy?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The Flow version and its tests are metadata you deploy. The Opportunities you Debug are data. Deploying v4 does not create last week’s Tasks.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Change sets move one version. Test records stay behind unless you seed LAB_ data. I never use production customer rows as the first Debug. Fault logs created in tests are data to delete. AUTO-012 migrate is also metadata; this lesson is how that metadata is versioned and shipped.
interview_questions.example: Retrieving the Flow XML does not include production Task rows.
tradeoffs: Seed data in sandbox vs empty Debug
follow_ups: Do Flow tests travel in the change set?

interview_questions.question: A director wants you to ‘hot-fix the Flow in production now.’ How do you answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I reproduce in sandbox, fix, Debug, test, deploy, and Activate in production. I will not start by saving over the live version without a version plan and a rollback version.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I acknowledge severity. I still compare versions and fault messages first—maybe Activate was forgotten (this lesson) or entry criteria (AUTO-010). If a true fix is needed, I use the theater: do not rewrite the script mid-show; put a new cast on after rehearsal. I keep the prior version to reactivate. I mention in-flight interviews. I do not Debug on the customer’s Opportunity as the design environment.
interview_questions.example: Production Inactive v4; the ‘bug’ is a missed Activate, not a canvas error.
tradeoffs: Reactivate prior version vs forward fix
weak_answer_warnings: Yes, I edit production first every time
